translation: Pallavi (Chorus): See the endless heaps of sorrow of the flame-of-the-forest flowers fallen to the ground; for our forsaken village there is no protector to come to its aid. See the endless heaps of sorrow of the flame-of-the-forest flowers fallen to the ground; for our forsaken village there is no protector to come to its aid. For the village raised with such tender love, the heart is full of gasping sobs; O rulers who don't care and can't bear to see us rise, our village is miles away from development. See the endless heaps of sorrow of the flame-of-the-forest flowers fallen to the ground; for our forsaken village there is no protector to come to its aid.

Verse 1: The chalky stream, its rocks laid bare, shows a path of thorns; seeing the potholes on the crooked road, the song in my heart cried out. We can't get across to the far bank; if there were a boat, the village could cross. How are we to reach the shore, sir? Why won't the government come to help? See the endless heaps of sorrow of the flame-of-the-forest flowers fallen to the ground; for our forsaken village there is no protector to come to its aid.

Verse 2: Pitch darkness has covered Mother Village, there is no light; what little we had went out the other day, and it became a new-moon night. At night the fireflies have become the torches that show the way; living in huts, a dim lamp has become our only friend. See the endless heaps of sorrow of the flame-of-the-forest flowers fallen to the ground; for our forsaken village there is no protector to come to its aid.

Verse 3: For our scattered lives, Mother Forest became our support; the cool, cool breezes became our lullaby and cradle. Leaves and wild greens filled our bellies, water from springs dug in the sand quenched our thirst; ours are ruined lives, show pity and take us in. See the endless heaps of sorrow of the flame-of-the-forest flowers fallen to the ground; for our forsaken village there is no protector to come to its aid.

Verse 4: For the once-bustling village, tears have become its springs; it has become a whirlpool of hardship, every meal a crisis. Look, in the struggle to survive, the village has become a noose; under fascist rule, the lives of the poor have become a burden. See the endless heaps of sorrow of the flame-of-the-forest flowers fallen to the ground; for our forsaken village there is no protector to come to its aid.

Verse 5: There isn't a drop of drinking water; see the struggle of the people of the soil. With not a drop coming from the borewell, the village wept aloud. Wiping away Mother Village's tears, taking her soil and placing it on our foreheads as a bottu, for a change in these lives of forced labour we will stand up to the ruler. See the endless heaps of sorrow of the flame-of-the-forest flowers fallen to the ground; for our forsaken village there is no protector to come to its aid. summaryEn:
Nela Ralina Modugha Poovu ("The Flame-of-the-Forest Flower Fallen to the Ground") is filed under Social Tragedy. It is a song of protest and grief for a neglected village. The chorus takes the modugu (flame-of-the-forest) blossom, a bright red flower common in the Telangana countryside, fallen and lying in the dust, as an image for the village's heaps of sorrow. It complains that no protector comes to help and accuses the "rulers" of keeping the village miles away from development.

Each verse lists a missing basic need. There is no road across the dried, rocky stream and no boat to cross it. There is no electricity, so fireflies serve as torches and a dim lamp is the only friend in the hut. There is no drinking water, and even the borewell yields not a drop. Uprooted families survive on forest leaves and on water from springs dug in the sand, and every meal is a crisis. The tone hardens as the song goes on: it speaks of "fascist rule" and of "lives of forced labour" (vetti). In the last verse the villagers wipe Mother Village's tears, put her soil on their foreheads as a bottu, and vow to stand up to their rulers. The long, returning chorus gives the song the sweep of a public lament that is also a call to action.

నేల రాలిన మోదుగు పూవు అనేది సామాజిక విషాద గీతాల విభాగంలో చేర్చిన పాట. నిర్లక్ష్యానికి గురైన పల్లె కోసం పాడిన నిరసన, దుఃఖం కలిసిన గీతం ఇది. తెలంగాణ పల్లెల్లో విరివిగా కనిపించే ఎర్రని మోదుగు పూలు నేల రాలి మట్టిలో పడి ఉండటాన్ని పల్లవి ఊరి పుట్టెడు బాధలకు ప్రతీకగా తీసుకుంటుంది. దిక్కులేని మా పల్లెను ఆదుకునే నాథుడే లేడని వాపోతూ, అభివృద్ధికి మా ఊరిని ఆమడ దూరంలో ఉంచిన పాలకులను నిలదీస్తుంది.

ప్రతి చరణం ఒక్కో కనీస అవసరం లేని దుస్థితిని చెబుతుంది: రాళ్ళు తేలిన వాగు మీద దారి లేదు, దాటడానికి ఓడ లేదు; కరెంటు లేక మిణుగురు పురుగులే దివిటీలయ్యాయి, గుడిసెలో గుడ్డిదీపమే నేస్తమైంది; తాగడానికి మంచినీళ్ళు లేవు, బోరు నుంచి చుక్క కూడా రాదు. చెదిరిపోయిన బతుకులు అడవి ఆకులు, అలములు, చెలిమె నీళ్ళతో గడుపుతున్నాయి; పూటపూటకూ గండమే. పాట సాగేకొద్దీ స్వరం కఠినమవుతుంది — "ఫాసిస్టు పాలన", "వెట్టి బతుకులు" అనే మాటలు వినిపిస్తాయి. చివరి చరణంలో పల్లె తల్లి కన్నీళ్ళు తుడిచి, ఆమె మట్టిని బొట్టుగా పెట్టుకుని, మార్పు కోసం ఏలేవాళ్ళను ఎదిరిస్తామని ప్రజలు ప్రతిజ్ఞ చేస్తారు. పదే పదే తిరిగివచ్చే పొడవైన పల్లవి ఈ పాటను ఒక సామూహిక విలాపంగానూ, అదే సమయంలో పోరాటానికి పిలుపుగానూ నిలబెడుతుంది.
